id: # perfhost: what the host-side performance lane found while measuring the pipeline (csrc/runtime/pipe_bench)

cause: the device mesher (cuda/mesh, render_blocks.c compiled for the device) reads address 0xc (a NULL pointer plus 12) inside render_block while explore-long-s1 envs walk into new terrain with groups of 4 or more envs a stream: every render after it fails (cumesh: counts: an illegal memory access; curender: the device mesher failed); never seen with groups of 1 (N 2, 400 steps); the host meshes the same sections. lane/meshcrash: the same class as renderprec-anvil-cumesh is likely (a draw leaves a warp split; the run kernels' overflow redraw fed unsynced shuffles: meshcrash-run-overflow-shfl, both fixed in a5fefea0), not proven: on the GPU host GPU 1, explore N 128 --env-seeds 50+300 steps, the fix and master 5cfcd77a both ran clean 10 of 10 and memcheck on the N 8 repro found 0 errors with the fix, so this set does not reproduce it
repro: pipe_bench --kinds explore --ns 128 --device-mesh 1 --env-seeds (full 100+1000 corpus, the GPU host; lane/popspeed saw 1 in 10 die); compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck out/runtime/pipe_bench --kinds explore --ns 8 -j 8 --device-mesh 1 --steps 150 --warm 2 (Invalid __global__ read of size 4 at $cumesh_run$render_block+0xaf1e0, address 0xc)

cause: play's view read a falling block copy's light (thing_light) from the server world with World.getFullBlockLightValue, which loads a chunk that is not loaded: where the client still drew the copy after the server had let its chunk go, the frame generated that chunk and the next row's block changes moved (2 against 3 at row 10322); the pool alone replays it exactly, so only the pipeline (the view beside the tick) diverged. The read now takes the client world there, as the vanilla client does
